newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Dutch prepare EU farm price compromise.
newsitem.headline: Dutch prepare EU farm price compromise.

text.p: Dutch Agriculture Minister Jozias Van Aartsen was due to present a compromise farm price package for next year after ministers strongly opposed plans to slash aid to wheat farmers and called for "sweeteners", EU officials said on Tuesday.

On Monday, the first day of the annual EU farm price marathon, 12 of the 15 farm ministers attacked a proposal to cut payments to cereals farmers by 1.4 billion ecus ($1.6 billion) to help fund aid for beef producers hit by the mad cow crisis.

They disputed a claim by EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler that cereals farmers were over-compensated for cuts in support prices and said there was enough spare cash in the 1997 farm budget to help the beef farmers.

Fischler said the aid could be adjusted to match price changes and added that there was no room in the 1998 budget to compensate farmers after a fall in prices due to the health scare over bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE).
Afterwards, Van Aartsen and Fischler held a lengthy series of private meetings with farm ministers in which the long lists of concessions they are seeking to please farmers back home were discussed.
Requests ranged from easing penalties for cereals farmers who planted too much grain to increased milk production quotas.
Nearly all countries called for an immediate decision on how much land cereals farmers must set aside in 1998 in order to claim aid payments.
Ireland and Finland sought special measures to help sheep farmers while Mediterranean countries called for extra aid for wine, olive oil and tomato producers.
Fischler said he was disappointed with the "wish lists" which complicated what was an otherwise straightforward price package with few changes.
It was too early to fix the 1998 set-aside rate as the harvest picture was still unclear, he added.
